items.stem: An AI demand signal predicts a sharp sales jump next week. Before changing the plan, what should the planner do first?

options.text: Check the drivers behind the signal against known demand events
options.rationale: Correct: verifying the cause prevents over-reacting to a spurious signal.
Acting on an unverified signal can cause costly excess.

options.text: Ignore the signal because AI is unreliable
options.rationale: Dismissing it outright wastes a potentially useful input; verify instead.

items.explanation: Correct: verifying the cause prevents over-reacting to a spurious signal.

items.stem: Which TWO data problems would most undermine AI-assisted planning? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Inaccurate master data such as wrong lead times
options.rationale: Correct: bad master data propagates into every AI recommendation.

options.text: Large gaps in historical demand records
options.rationale: Correct: missing history weakens the AI's basis for prediction.
Clean data helps planning rather than harming it.
Accurate counts improve, not undermine, planning.

items.explanation: Correct: bad master data propagates into every AI recommendation.

items.stem: An AI routing tool proposes a route that passes a bridge too low for the vehicle. What does this illustrate?

options.text: AI output needs human review against real-world constraints it may not know
options.rationale: Correct: AI can miss physical constraints, so human checks remain essential.

options.text: AI routing should always be followed exactly
options.rationale: Following an unsafe route blindly is the error being illustrated.

options.text: Physical constraints never matter in routing
options.rationale: Physical constraints are precisely what matter here.
Vehicle data is central to a valid route.

items.explanation: Correct: AI can miss physical constraints, so human checks remain essential.
